0.23.content: If you sign in with a **Quillium account**, we now link your anonymous analytics identifier to that account so we can better help troubleshoot issues you report. This only kicks in once you deliberately create an account — the anonymous experience for everyone else is unchanged, and nothing about past analytics is affected. See the updated [Privacy Policy](https://quillium.bryanhu.com/privacy) for details.

0.22.content:
# Undo history
Your **undo history** just got a whole lot more robust.

A consequence of this is that documents now begin each session with a **fresh undo stack** by default. If you prefer undo to survive app restarts, enable **Settings → Editor → Undo after restart for new documents**; the choice applies to documents you create afterward. Documents created before July 14, 2026 keep their cross-restart undo behavior.

# UI changes
The **drafts panel** is resizable now—drag its edge, resize it with the arrow keys, or use the corner button to expand it to the available width, useful once your draft names get long.

![The drafts panel widened to show full draft names, with its resize handle and full-width toggle visible](/changelog/0.22.png)

A few more changes round out this release.
# Other changes
1. You can **duplicate a document** straight from the library—press `D` on a card or use the preview panel—which copies over its comments and revisions as an independent document.

2. **Deleted tabs** now show up correctly as read-only history instead of silently falling back to another tab.
3. Floating comments and revisions no longer cover the draft tree or sign-in controls. Authorship Playback now tells human, AI, and mixed-authorship revisions apart correctly.
4. And starting a new tab is easier to find—its button is always visible, with a `Cmd/Ctrl+T` shortcut and a File menu entry.

5. Finally, there's a beta **Sign in with ChatGPT** option under AI Settings powered by [OpenAI OAuth](https://github.com/EvanZhouDev/openai-oauth/), for connecting your ChatGPT account instead of an API key.

0.21.content:
When you share a **read-only web page** of your writing, keeping it current used to mean remembering to publish again after every change. Now Quillium can **update the public page for you**. Once your edits settle, it quietly republishes the latest version, so anyone with the link always sees your most recent draft. You decide how long it waits before refreshing, and you can switch back to publishing by hand whenever you'd rather do it yourself.

In the editor, typing **`---` on its own line** now draws a clean **horizontal rule** instead of leaving the dashes as plain text. The raw markers reappear the moment your cursor lands on that line — the same way headings reveal their formatting — so breaking a document into sections stays effortless.

![A horizontal rule dividing two sections of a document](/changelog/0.21.png)

Drafts are more flexible too. You can now **branch a new version straight from your original draft**, not just from later ones, making it easier to explore a fresh direction from the very start. And the **root of a storyline is now protected** from deletion, so the foundation your other versions build on can't be removed by accident.

0.20.content:
Quillium now tracks **how a document was written**, not just what it says — distinguishing the words you **typed** from the passages you **pasted** in. Useful when a student, applicant, or writer needs to show the work is genuinely theirs.

![Authorship playback replaying a draft, color-coded by where each edit came from](/changelog/0.20.png)

Open it from the status bar or View menu to **replay your draft coming together step by step**, color-coded by where each edit came from, with a scrubber and play/pause/speed controls.

0.19.content:
Documents now hold **tabs** along the top, so a single piece of work can keep its main draft and its side notes together in one place instead of scattered across the library.

Drafts also gained two clearer ways to move forward. **Iterate** carries a draft into its next version and tidies the earlier one away, keeping a long chain of revisions as a clean, readable list. **Branch** spins off a different take on the same idea and keeps both alive side by side, so you can explore an alternative without losing the original.

The library gained a proper **search box**: start typing and Quillium finds the right document across everything you've written, with matching text highlighted so you can spot what you were looking for at a glance.

In the editor, **comments now travel with your text** — cut or copy a passage and paste it elsewhere, and the notes attached to it come along instead of being left behind.

Finally, the **What's New button** is now always within reach, with a dropdown to revisit the notes from any past release whenever you want to look back.

0.18.content:
You can now open **multiple windows** at once — keep two documents side by side, or reference one draft while you write another, without juggling tabs.

The **annotation sidebar** has a roomier **two-column layout** when you're writing without the assistant panel, so your comments and notes have more space to breathe.

Formatting got richer too: **Markdown headings now go all the way down to the smallest sizes**, giving you finer control over how you structure longer documents.

Finally, sending us a **bug report** is now separate from sharing general **feedback**, so it's clearer how to reach us depending on what's on your mind.

0.17.content:
The **annotation sidebar** is easier to adjust while you write. The resize handle now sits on the side where you expect it, and a new reset button makes it simple to get back to the default layout.

We've also cleaned up a few **interface details**: the font guide no longer shows Inter where it does not belong, and the dictionary shortcut hint now points to the right keyboard command.

0.16.content:
**Export from the editor status bar**, manage **document tags** from the library preview, and stack related **dictionary lookups** without losing context.

Also: resizable annotation sidebar, easier AI panel resize handles, and Markdown bold/italic shortcuts now toggle off when text is already formatted.

0.15.content:
Quillium now has a **Markdown rich text mode** for writers who like Markdown shortcuts but still want a polished editing surface. The formatting controls are the same as Google Docs (e.g. Command+B for bolding on macOS), and you can make markdown headers. The keyboard shortcut for pulling up the dictionary has been changed.

You can also **export to PDF** directly from Quillium. When you need to share a finished draft, archive a copy, or send work somewhere that expects a fixed layout, PDF export is now built into the app.

Finally, **web sharing** is now functional for those who have a Quillium/Omni account. *Join the waitlist at quillium.bryanhu.com/omni*

0.14.content:
This update lays the groundwork for **Quillium Omni**, our upcoming [sync and real-time collaboration service](https://quillium.bryanhu.com/blog/introducing-omni).

You may see new Omni surfaces in the app while we keep access in waitlist mode and continue developing hosted pieces. Don't worry, Omni will always be explicitly opt-in (you have to pay for it, after all). This means that **local writing still works exactly as before** when Omni is not enabled.

As with our [commitment to privacy](https://quillium.bryanhu.com/blog/quillium-privacy), we will *never* send your documents to our servers unless you ask for it.

0.13.content:
Quillium now includes a built-in **grammar and spelling checker** powered by Harper. Misspellings show red squiggles, grammar issues show blue — click any underlined word to see suggestions and apply fixes with one click. You can add words to your personal dictionary, ignore individual suggestions, or mute all suggestions when you want to write distraction-free.

Configure the checker in **Settings → Grammar** — choose your English dialect (American, British, Australian, or Canadian) or disable it entirely.

0.12.content:
This update brings a new **writing statistics** panel — open it from the toolbar to see word count breakdowns, readability scores, and more about your document.

Behind the scenes, we've strengthened **error recovery** for deeply nested annotations. The app now catches cases where nested content could be silently lost and offers to restore it.

We've also reworded our **privacy policy** for clarity — nothing functional changed, just better legal language.
